description: Room reverb built by simulation: four audio sources played through speakers in a virtual room, picked up by four microphones, with the room's size and wall material under CV

params.text: Level of that source in the room; the halo drawn round its node grows with it
The left-right position of that source, dragged by its yellow node in the room display
The forward-back position of that source, dragged by its yellow node in the room display
The left-right position of that destination, dragged by its white node in the room display; destination positions take no CV
The forward-back position of that destination, dragged by its white node in the room display
Drag the number up or down to set the room's width, anywhere from 1m to 300m
Drag the number up or down to set the room's length, anywhere from 1m to 300m
Drag the number up or down to set the room's height, anywhere from 2m to 100m
Frequency of the high-pass filter applied every time sound reflects off a wall; at the 10Hz minimum the wall reflects the low end unfiltered
Frequency of the low-pass filter applied every time sound reflects off a wall; at the 22kHz maximum the wall reflects the top end unfiltered
How much of the sound comes back off a wall: at 0% none does and the module becomes a plain spatialiser, at 100% with both filters wide open the sound reverberates without end
Roughness of the wall surface: at 0% sound reflects at an equal angle, at 100% at random angles and time offsets, which smooths the decay of sharp transients

inputs.text: Audio into that source, which puts a numbered yellow node in the room display
Moves that source left and right, 10V peak-to-peak covering the width of the room whatever its size
Moves that source forward and back, 10V peak-to-peak covering the length of the room whatever its size
Cutoff of the wall's high-pass filter at a volt per octave
Cutoff of the wall's low-pass filter at a volt per octave
Modulates how much sound a wall reflects, 10V peak-to-peak covering the whole range
Modulates the roughness of the wall surface, 10V peak-to-peak covering the whole range

outputs.text: The audio picked up by that microphone in the room

notes: every source is 1.5m above the floor and every destination 1.2m, so a source and a destination at the same point never produce an infinite level
a source whose position is modulated draws a second, ghost node at the modulated position; drag the solid node, not the ghost
each destination in use costs 4 to 8% of a CPU core
Rack's own preset menu carries 31 factory rooms, eleven from VCV such as Bathroom, Arena and Vocal booth and twenty from Omri Cohen; the module has no right-click menu of its own
a source makes no sound in the room until audio is patched to its input, and the room is heard only through a microphone output, so at least one of each has to be patched
